newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Aug 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Senate President Ernesto Maceda said yesterday he was backing calls for an investigation of the country's oil firms for their recent increase in fuel prices. (STAR/INQUIRER)

- A seven-man Senate panel opens today its investigation on the extent of the drug problem in the country, including the alleged involvement of some government officials, lawmakers and law enforcers in the operations of drug lords. (BULLETIN)
- Scattered violence since Friday in Western Mindanao and a sea accident left at least 11 people dead, reports reaching the Police Regional Office in Zamboanga City said yesterday.
- Businessmen are strongly against the revived plan to slap taxes on foreign currency deposits because this will trigger massive capital flight to tax-haven countries.

- The Philippine central bank crafted new monetary targets for this year and next year after inputting the impact of higher interest rates. Based on confidential documents, the government is targetting a 16.5 percent growth in domestic liquidity from the original 19.9 percent expansion. (TODAY/BUSINESS DAILY/INQUIRER)

- Transportation and Communications Secretary Arturo Enrile bared plans to allow Bell Telecommunication Philippines Inc to operate in some unserved parts of Metro Manila and the country's economic zones. (INQUIRER/STAR)
